'''DecipherCon 2000''' was Decipher's second company convention, held 5–8 October 2000 at the Doubletree Resort and Conference Center in Kissimmee, Florida. It hosted the [[2000 Decipher World Championship|Star Wars CCG World Championship]], in which [[Matt Sokol]] defeated [[Yannick Lapointe]] in the Final Confrontation.<ref name="sched">[https://web.archive.org/web/20061009205800/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/ DecipherCon 2000 schedule], Decipher (Wayback 9 October 2006)</ref><ref name="jls3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001117011300/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/jls3.html Matt Sokol, 2000 Star Wars CCG World Champion!], Jean-Luc Simard, Decipher (Wayback 17 November 2000)</ref>

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 tournament hall.jpg|thumb|right|320px|Main tournament hall, 6 October 2000]]
[[File:DecipherCon 2000 SWCCG champion plaque.jpg|thumb|right|320px|Star Wars CCG 2000 World Champion plaque]]

The 1999 convention had been in Virginia Beach ([[DecipherCon 1999]]). Decipher billed 2000 as "the Whole Shebang": World Championship play, first looks at new product, and seminars inside product development.<ref name="home">[https://web.archive.org/web/20040217015645/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/ DecipherCon 2000], Decipher (Wayback 17 February 2004)</ref><ref name="tfn">[http://www.theforce.net/ccg/story/Decipher_Update_DecipherCon_2000_75291.asp Decipher Update: DecipherCon 2000], TheForce.net (5 September 2000)</ref>

== Venue and dates ==

* '''Dates:''' 5–8 October 2000 (Thursday–Sunday)
* '''Site:''' Doubletree Resort and Conference Center, Kissimmee, Florida (near Orlando)
* '''Master of ceremonies:''' Mark Tuttle, Decipher net representative<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="insider">''Star Wars Insider'' 52 (2000), "It's a CCG TKO When Star Wars Fans Compete at DecipherCon 2000"</ref>

World Championship constructed days ran Thursday through Saturday. Sunday held the team constructed event and remaining side tournaments.<ref name="sched" /><ref name="events">[https://web.archive.org/web/20081013224103/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/schedule/events.html DecipherCon master tournament schedule], Decipher (Wayback 13 October 2008)</ref>

== Guests ==

Special guests were [[Michonne Bourriague]] (Aurra Sing) and [[Shannon Baksa]] (Mara Jade). Both sat autograph tables during the weekend.<ref name="home" /><ref name="tfn" />

TheForce.net's September preview listed autograph sessions, Q&As, seminars (including a card-design seminar whose output was meant for a future expansion), and the first annual Decipher Olympics: sorting competitions, card-house building, and card tosses. Charles Hickey's trip report recorded a card flung the length of the hall into a chandelier.<ref name="tfn" /><ref name="hickey">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ mr-hickey-goes-to-florida], Charles "Teacher" Hickey, Decktech (14 October 2000)</ref>

Decipher had announced its ''The Lord of the Rings'' Trading Card Game licence on 10 August 2000. A LOTR TCG poster hung behind Baksa's signing table in the official photographs.

== Star Wars CCG World Championship ==

Full results, lists, and GEMP imports are on [[2000 Decipher World Championship]]. The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Death Star II]]. Sokol (United States) defeated Lapointe (Canada).<ref name="home" /><ref name="jls3" />

Wikipedia and ''Star Wars Insider'' 52 list 72 Day 1 players. Francis K. Lalumiere, writing from the floor on 5 October, put 170 competitors in the main hall fighting for a Day 2 seat. Sokol finished 36th on Day 1, then advanced through Day 2 and Day 3.<ref name="wp">[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game Star Wars Customizable Card Game], Wikipedia</ref><ref name="insider" /><ref name="fkl2">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010107221700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/fkl2.html Mighty Jabba Sails Across the Atlantic], Francis K. Lalumiere, Decipher (Wayback 7 January 2001)</ref><ref name="sokol-trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000)</ref>

Day 1 started hours late. Alex Tennet wrote that [[Peter DiBiasio]] went undefeated and won that day's Swiss. Several players were disqualified for deck-list errors, among them [[Jonny Chu]] (5–2 into game 8) and [[Steven Lewis]].<ref name="tennet">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cards], Alex "Greedo" Tennet, Decktech (13 October 2000)</ref><ref name="sokol-dt">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ sokols-dcon-2000-report], Matt Sokol, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref>

Justin Pakes ("Juz") directed the Star Wars rooms. Twelve players reached Day 3. Lapointe led that table 8 (+47); Sokol 6 (+23) took the second Final Confrontation seat.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="d3">[https://web.archive.org/web/20010303120030/http://decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/events/results/starwars3.html DecipherCon 2000 Day 3], Decipher (Wayback 3 March 2001)</ref>

[[Team Albany]] (including Sokol, [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Chris Terwilliger]], [[Jonny Chu]], Art Wright, and Aaron Kingery) built Sokol's Day 3 [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] list overnight. Sokol later won the Sunday team constructed event with Chu and both Terwilligers.<ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="sokol-trando" /><ref name="eltwigg">[https://x.com/swccg/status/1327607833836331009 Brian Terwilliger quoted by @swccg], 14 November 2020</ref>

== Star Wars CCG Final Confrontation ==

The match was played in a closed room with only Sokol, Lapointe, and judges. The audience watched on a large screen in an adjacent cinema-style room. [[Joe Alread]], [[Kyle Heuer]], and Kendrick Summers commentated.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="tennet" />

'''Game 1.''' Sokol [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] (X-wings / Numbers) against Lapointe [[Bring Him Before Me / Take Your Father's Place|Bring Him Before Me]]. Sokol's Light list had been turned in at 59 cards; he added [[Civil Disorder]] at registration and the deck had no Luke. Lapointe won by 20.<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="sokol-dt" /><ref name="lapointe">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-world-day-3-whos-the-man-not-med1324/ world-day-3-whos-the-man-not-me], Yannick "Crusher" Lapointe, Decktech (11 October 2000)</ref>

'''Game 2.''' Sokol [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] (walkers / Sandwhirl) against Lapointe's Super Falcon list. Sokol needed at least 21 Force of differential. Lapointe retrieved heavily with On The Edge / Off The Edge while Battle Order slowed Sokol's drains. An [[Abyssin Ornament]] left Sokol on 25 Life Force; Lapointe drew his last card. Combined score: Sokol 2 (+5), Lapointe 2 (−5).<ref name="jls3" /><ref name="tennet" /><ref name="lapointe" />

''Insider'' 52 called it the United States' first Worlds title since [[Matt Potter]] in 1998. Sokol told the magazine it was the first time he had beaten Lapointe, after many games since the Ottawa Grand Slam. Lapointe kept a Yoda doll at the table as a luck-bringer.<ref name="insider" />

== Final Confrontation video ==

Decipher streamed both games from the convention site (20 kb and 80 kb RealMedia). The Player's Council later posted the recording on YouTube (1 hour 21 minutes), with the original Alread / Heuer / Summers commentary.

[[File:DecipherCon 2000 Worlds Final still.jpg|640px|link=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q0sFxQ2i3Hk]]

* [https://youtu.be/jFXqTc1jkNc Matt Sokol interview] looking back at the match
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20080208131907/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/finals/index.html Original Decipher finals page] (Wayback 8 February 2008), with RealMedia links and championship deck URLs

Thursday's first-ever [[Jabba's Palace Sealed Deck]] product tournament drew 24 players in a side hall while Worlds Day 1 ran next door. Light Side dominated (Lapointe was the only Dark winner after game 1). [[Koen Meijssen]] (Holland) 8 (+69) beat [[Martin Akesson]] (Sweden) 6 (+17) in the final by 3 Force. Tournament director Jeff Weitkamp (Gold 40).<ref name="fkl2" />

== Photographs ==

Decipher posted a JavaScript gallery of about 166 photographs from 4–8 October 2000 (<code>/deciphercon/2000/photos/</code>). Thumbnail clicks opened pop-up pages; crawlers mostly missed the full JPEGs. == Trip reports ==

Official Decipher "Zoom In" copy came from Francis K. Lalumiere, Jean-Luc Simard, Marcus Sheppard, and John Kaufeld. The Star Wars pieces are Lalumiere's Jabba's Palace Sealed report and Simard's Final Confrontation report.<ref name="reports">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001116233700/http://www.decipher.com/deciphercon/2000/reports/index.html DecipherCon 2000 reports], Decipher (Wayback 16 November 2000)</ref>

Player reports went up on Decktech within days:

* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-sokols-dcon-2000-reportd1327/ Matt Sokol] — all three Worlds days, [[Team Albany]], the missing Luke, and the Final Confrontation
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-11-world-day-3-whos-the-man-not-med1324/ Yannick Lapointe] — Day 3 table, Super Falcon vs Sokol, and the Final Confrontation
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-13-deciphercon-2000-juz-beer-and-cardsd1338/ Alex Tennet] — UK travel, [[Team OK-UK]] shirts, Day 1 games, DQs, and watching the final
* [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-10-14-mr-hickey-goes-to-floridad1343/ Charles Hickey] — Endor crew, card toss, Day 1 games
* [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], Trandosite, 25 October 2000 (Rod Latham / Alex Tennet)
* Decktech also carried reports from [[Dominic Gaudreault]], [[Brian Terwilliger]], [[Bastian Winkelhaus]], Doug Faust, [[Martin Akesson]], [[Mike Kessling]], Tim Guzman, and others, indexed from [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/tournament_reports/ the tournament-reports list] under 8–15 October 2000

== Other games at the convention ==

The same weekend also held World Championships for ''Star Trek'' CCG (Eric Johnfauno over Brian Sykes) and Young Jedi (Ian Vincent over Philippe Parise), plus more than 60 side tournaments.<ref name="home" /><ref name="insider" />
